source.title: RWKV: Reinventing RNNs for the Transformer Era
source.authors: Bo Peng; Eric Alcaide; Quentin Anthony; Alon Albalak; Samuel Arcadinho; Stella Biderman; Huan-Qi Cao; Xin Cheng; Michael Chung; Matteo Grella; GV KranthiKiran; Xingjian Du; Xu-Zheng He; Haowen Hou; Przemyslaw Kazienko; Jan Kocoń; Jiaming Kong; Bartlomiej Koptyra; Hayden Lau; Krishna Sri Ipsit Mantri; Ferdinand Mom; Atsushi Saito; Xiangru Tang; Bo-Lun Wang; J. record.tranche_reason: The study tests scaling-law behavior with a different model architecture, RWKV, using a scaling sweep and loss-versus-compute fits.
record.gate_note: The scaling-law section reports a 45-model sweep and quantitative fit results. Other reported results include downstream benchmark comparisons, Enwik8 perplexity, and test loss after extended-context fine-tuning; these do not test the versions about downstream predictability, other modalities or regimes, or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. The benchmark plots show performance by compute but do not report a fitted or otherwise quantified prediction relationship.
record.test_reason: The study fits pretraining loss against compute for 45 RWKV language models trained on the Pile. This applies the original loss-versus-compute method to a new architecture, a linear-attention RNN, and checks the fit on runs one order of magnitude beyond the fitted range. T3 fits better than T2: the method is the same as the original, and only the setting (architecture) is new.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that RWKV, unlike what Kaplan et al. report for LSTMs, follows the same general scaling-law form as transformers: r2 0.994 on Pareto-optimal points and r2 0.875 when extrapolated one further order of magnitude.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a comparable loss-versus-compute scaling analysis, but applies it to RWKV rather than transformer models and sweeps dataset-parameter pairs.
record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The fit results are reported with r2 values but no uncertainty estimates. The text does not specify the individual sweep settings or clearly describe which runs were used for fitting and extrapolation.
record.rows_left_out: No scaling-law rows left out. Downstream benchmark curves are not recorded as rows because the paper reports comparisons by compute, not a quantified test of downstream prediction from scale or pretraining loss.

untested.parts: Separate power laws in parameters or in tokens. No exponents are reported.
Extrapolation over several orders of magnitude (only one is tested). Extrapolation of parameter or token curves.
All parts: no compute-optimal N/D allocation is fitted.
All parts: no shape ablation at fixed parameter count.
All parts: loss scaling is reported only for text pretraining.
All parts: benchmark accuracy is plotted against compute, but no predictive relationship is fitted.
All parts: no comparison of fitting choices or exponents.

record.verdict_notes: Compute is computed with the standard 6ND approximation. The 45 sweep settings are not listed. No uncertainty or exponents are given. The downstream accuracy-versus-compute plots (Figs. 1, 5, 12) are comparisons with transformers, not quantified predictions, so they do not test V6.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests loss versus compute on Pareto-optimal RWKV runs; it does not report separate power-law tests versus parameter count or token count, or tests of when each is non-bottlenecking.
The reported extrapolation is for the loss-versus-compute curve; the study does not report small-run extrapolation tests for parameter-count or token-count curves.

rows.subject: RWKV models
rows.operation_detail: Fit loss as a function of compute over a sweep of dataset-parameter pairs.
rows.measure: r2 for the linear fit to the loss-versus-compute scaling curve
rows.note: The authors report this fit for the Pareto-optimal points; the section describes the scaling-law curve as having the general form established for transformers.
rows.check: The measure is r2 of a linear fit to Pareto-optimal points on log-log axes. 'Log-log' is implied by the authors' contrast with LSTMs' 'log-log linear scaling'. No fitted exponent is reported. The compute range in Fig. 4 spans about 10^-1 to 10^3 exaFLOP. Baseline 'not stated' is correct.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.2, paragraph immediately preceding Figure 4: 45 RWKV models; Pareto-optimal linear-fit r²=0.994.

rows.subject: RWKV models
rows.operation_detail: Extrapolate the loss-versus-compute curve by an additional order of magnitude.
rows.measure: r2 for the extrapolated curve fit
rows.note: The text describes the extrapolated fit as extremely good. It does not specify in text which individual runs were used to fit the curve or to assess the extrapolation.
rows.check: The extrapolation covers only one additional order of magnitude. r2 falls from 0.994 (fit) to 0.875 (test points), although the authors call it 'extremely good'. Which runs are test points is shown only by colour in Fig. 4. A reader could treat this as weaker than full support.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.2, final sentence preceding Figure 4: extrapolation by one additional order of magnitude, r²=0.875.

relationships.display_finding: The log-log linear fit to the loss-compute Pareto frontier achieved R² of 0.994 across about four orders of magnitude in compute.
